fix(mission): unify queue-position reporting with the real matcher (J1)

Review finding J1 (full-branch review, m-2026-09-08-004 round 3),
HIGHEST PRIORITY: K8's fix computed a pending dispatch's reported queue
position via a bare Worker-equality filter, while matchDispatchPending
itself additionally skips-and-clears stale entries and skips
unresolvable ones (K1). The two could disagree: an unresolvable entry
ahead of a fresh dispatch was reported as "ahead of it and will be
matched first" when the matcher would actually skip that entry and
match the fresh one instead -- the message told the operator the exact
opposite of what happens. Both of K8's own pinning tests used two
resolvable, open missions, the one case where a naive filter and the
real matcher agree -- the same fixture-guarding shape J2 will separately
flag in the drift guard.

Extracted the classification into internal/mission:
PendingEntryStatus/ClassifyPendingEntry/ClassifyPendingDispatches is now
the single source of truth for "which pending dispatches for a worker
would actually be matched." matchDispatchPending (internal/hook) and
the new exported hook.DispatchBoundMessage both call it, so the entry
the hook would match and the position reported to the operator cannot
diverge. hook.DispatchBoundMessage also collapses what was ~30
duplicated lines between the CLI's bindDispatchedMission and the MCP
twin into one shared implementation -- both surfaces had drifted once
already (K8) from maintaining two independent copies.

TestMissionDispatch_UnresolvableAheadEntryNotReportedAsBlocking
reproduces the leader's own captured scenario (an unresolvable m-800
ahead of a fresh dispatch) and asserts the fresh dispatch is reported
as first in queue, not blocked by an entry the matcher would skip.
Confirmed failing against a targeted mutation reproducing the pre-J1
bare-filter behavior (reverted after confirming, then restored).
EOF
)"
